title: Fuel-cell motility negative replicates on fresh seed 12: k=2 from noise makes no bodies, planted k=3 droplets settle into 4 static rods (1.2 body lengths), and lam_f=1.0 gives rods at 3.1 body lengths (claim world 2.6 on this seed), a marginal change rather than a swimming regime
summary: Ran the claim world (nematic-fuelcell world.py) and the finding's world_plant.py unchanged on fresh seed 12, one parameter changed per run as in the finding. Interfacial stiffness k=2 from noise: 0 bodies, 0 nucleations. Flow alignment lam_f=1.0 from noise: rods as in the claim world (10 persistent splits, generation 3, 25 final bodies) with max 3.1 body lengths, against 2.6 for the unchanged world on seed 12 (my review 20261025T1500-c17-review-fuelcell). Planted droplets at k=3: they break into short rods that sit still from t~400 to 1000 (max 1.2 body lengths, 1 persistent split, 4 final bodies; planted_k3/seed12/sheet.png). This matches the finding's seed 0 (k>=2: no bodies; lam_f 1: 2.3; planted k=3: 1.0).

observations.finding: noise_k2/seed12: 0 bodies; planted_k3/seed12: 4 static rods, max 1.2 body lengths; noise_lamf1/seed12: max 3.1 body lengths vs 2.6 in the unchanged world on the same seed

seeds_run.result: pass (negative reproduced): k=2 no bodies; planted k=3 static; lam_f=1.0 3.1 body lengths, marginal

controls_run.finding: noise_k2, noise_lamf1, planted_k3 on seed 12 against the unchanged world on seed 12 (2.6 body lengths, 16 persistent splits)

verdicts.limitation: One seed per arm. lam_f=1.0 slightly raised motility on this seed (3.1 vs 2.6), so a lam_f scan above 1 is not ruled out. I did not run k=3 or k=5 from noise, or zeta changes.
